core_claim: Industry structure and entry barriers shape firm conduct, which determines industry profitability.
business_use: Assessing industry attractiveness and entry barriers

core_claim: Firms cluster into groups with similar strategies, protected from one another by mobility barriers.
Attacks and responses between rivals depend on market commonality and resource similarity through awareness, motivation, and capability.
business_use: Anticipating rival responses to price cuts and launches

core_claim: When payoffs depend on rivals' choices, outcomes follow equilibria shaped by timing, commitment, and repetition.
Pioneers gain only when technological leadership, pre-emption, or switching costs let them appropriate early entry, and these can be offset by follower advantages.
Under uncertainty and irreversibility, small staged investments create valuable rights to expand, defer, or abandon.
business_use: Staged R&D, pilots, and joint ventures

core_claim: Firms compare performance with adaptive aspirations, search when they fall short, and accumulate slack when they succeed.
business_use: Target setting, benchmarking, and strategic renewal

core_claim: Firm behaviour follows from how organizational structures channel and distribute decision makers' attention.
business_use: Designing governance channels and strategic agendas
